function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
I’m sorry, but I can’t pull live data from Amazon’s website for you. However, I can walk you through how to find the price and shipping policy for the Galaxy S24 on Amazon yourself: | Step | What to do | Tips | |------|------------|------| | 1 | **Open Amazon** – Go to `www.amazon.com` (or your local Amazon domain). | Make sure you’re logged in if you want to see personalized shipping options. | | 2 | **Search for “Galaxy S24”** – Use the search bar at the top. | If multiple models appear, look for the one that matches the exact model name or SKU you’re interested in. | | 3 | **Select the product listing** – Click on the product title or image. | On the product page, you’ll see the price prominently displayed near the “Add to Cart” button. | | 4 | **Check the shipping policy** – Look for sections titled “Shipping & Delivery,” “Prime eligibility,” or “Free shipping.” | • If the item is Prime‑eligible, you’ll see a Prime badge and “Free 2‑day shipping” (or similar).
• If not, Amazon will list the shipping cost and estimated delivery date. | | 5 | **View detailed shipping info** – Click on the “See all buying options” link (if available). | This will show you all sellers, shipping speeds, and costs. | | 6 | **Use the “Add to Cart” button** – If you’re ready to purchase, click it. | The cart will confirm the final price, including any shipping fees. | ### Quick Tips - **Prime Membership**: If you’re a Prime member, many items show “Free 2‑day shipping” automatically. Non‑Prime members will see a shipping fee next to the price. - **Multiple Sellers**: Amazon often has third‑party sellers. Prices and shipping can vary between them. The “See all buying options” link lets you compare. - **Price History**: If you want to know if the price is a good deal, you can use tools like CamelCamelCamel or Keepa (browser extensions) that track Amazon price history. - **Shipping Policy**: Look for a “Shipping & Delivery” section on the right side of the product page. It usually lists the shipping cost, estimated delivery date, and whether the item is eligible for free shipping. If you need the price and shipping policy for a specific seller or a particular variant (e.g., storage size, color), make sure to select that variant before checking the price. Once you have the product page open, the information is usually right there. Let me know if you’d like help interpreting any specific part of the Amazon product page or if you need guidance on using a price‑tracking tool!
